term: innovating cause, cause of coming to be
definition: A cause other than the thing itself from which that thing’s coming to be takes its origin. CausesOrigin c x is the primitive relation for this source reading; the reading of SCG I.13 requires such a c for what comes to be anew. It does not identify the cause as God, identify it with moving in an arbitrary respect, or equate beginning with being present at a first instant.
note: Typed parameter location: CausesOrigin : Being → Being → Prop in WhatComesToBeAnewHasInnovatingCauseReading. That usage-site reading is a constraining premise, not a definition of that primitive relation. Its witness separately satisfies c ≠ x; distinctness is not built into every CausesOrigin edge by the parameter type. The intended originating-cause interpretation remains OPEN. Audit #1233: the primary locator now names CauseFrame.CausesOrigin, a primitive relation field, rather than the quantified reading. This change supplies no definition body, structural law or bridge.

formal_gap.meaning: CauseFrame.CausesOrigin c x says that x's coming to be takes its origin from c: c is a cause of x's beginning, read from SCG I.13 for what comes to be anew. It is a supplied binary relation between beings, with no respect argument. It does not say that c continues to sustain x, that c is God, or that c moves x in some respect.
examples: A craftsman from whom a newly made artifact comes to be.
Parents from whom a child comes to be, read as origin only.
exclusions: Mere simultaneous presence with x, or conservation of an x that already exists.
Causing x's being (CausesIn at esse) and moving x in a respect (MovesIn): separate senses in DISAMB-CAUSE and DISAMB-COMING-TO-BE.
Being present at a first instant: beginning is not equated with existing at an earliest time.
open_obligations: Distinctness of cause and effect is not built into the relation: the reading WhatComesToBeAnewHasInnovatingCauseReading asserts a witness c with c ≠ x as a separate conjunct.
Transitivity, asymmetry and well-foundedness are not assumed.
The originating-cause interpretation and its applicability to real beginnings remain OPEN; the finite-past result does not identify the cause as God.
No formalization candidate: defining it from a time order and the existence predicate would replace a causal relation by a temporal one.
